Alex — quick update from my side after trying to reproduce locally:

- I used your payload and Node SDK 1.4.0 with a static API key (simulating your header). I hit a 502 error consistently when batch size > 32 for your payload shape (each item ~1.8K tokens).
- When I increased the SDK timeout to 30s and enabled exponential backoff (retries 3, base 500ms), the calls eventually succeed but latency is high and throughput suffers.
- Logs show an internal upstream timeout (502) from the model shard — looks like request fanout causes one shard to exceed its concurrency window for large batches.

Next steps I propose:
- Short-term: reduce recommended default batch size for Finlytics workload to 16 and increase client timeout to 30s + retries.
- Medium-term: we'll check autoscaler thresholds and whether we can route your requests across more shards (requires config change on Dedicated pool).

Can you try the smaller batch + timeout change and report back? I'll keep digging into routing and shard-concurrency logs.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Alex / team — Neha from support here with a short repro & recommendations after looking through the shard logs and your attached payload. Summary:

Root cause: combined effect of large per-item token count (~1.8K), high client batch size (64), and synchronous embed->rerank pipeline causing request fanout across 3 model shards. One shard hit internal queue timeout which surfaced as 502/504 to client.

Immediate mitigations (what to change in client):
- Set client batch_size = 16 (or tokens-per-batch <= 50K tokens).
- Set request timeout = 30000 ms and enable exponential backoff (retries=3).
- Split embed and rerank into two async calls where possible: 1) get embeddings, 2) call reranker with precomputed embeddings. This reduces real-time fanout.

Server-side actions we're taking:
- Increasing autoscaler headroom for your Dedicated pool during your trial window.
- Adjusting routing policy to prefer cross-shard fanout minimization for your account (opt-in change).
- Creating JIRA FIN-7235 to track a longer-term fix to improve cross-shard aggregation.

Repro steps we used (attached):
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @repro-payload-embed.json --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30
2) Observe 502 when batch_size >= 32 for the attached payload (each item ~1.8K tokens).

I'll open a support window for a live debugging session if you'd like; suggest Thurs 02/14 10:00 PT. Also attaching the server log excerpt and the exact payload we used.

Action items:
- Alex: test client-side mitigations (batch_size 16, timeout 30s) and report latency/throughput numbers.
- Marissa: include SLA language around recommended tokens-per-batch and routing behavior in the procurement checklist.
- Camila/Dylan/Neha: follow up on routing opt-in change and update JIRA FIN-7235.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call to walk through the logs live.

Neha Kapoor
